title: Accelerated Inorganic Materials Design with Generative AI Agents
experiments_summary: The study implements and evaluates MatAgent, a feedback-driven iterative framework. The following methods and experiments were conducted: (1) Dataset Construction: The MP-60 dataset was built from Materials Project crystal structures with up to 60 atoms per unit cell, energy above hull ≤0.02 eV/atom, excluding all-gaseous-element structures and those with lattice vectors >20 Å, yielding 48,323 structures split 6:2:2 for train/validation/test. (2) Crystal Structure Estimation: DiffCSP, a diffusion-based model, was trained on MP-60 to conditionally generate crystal structures from compositions. For each proposed reduced composition, five structures were generated for formula units Z=1 to 4, capped at 34 total atoms per unit cell. (3) Property Evaluation: iComFormer, a GNN-based transformer, was trained on MP-60 to predict formation energy per atom. The structure with the lowest predicted formation energy among generated candidates was selected as the most stable. (4) Knowledge Base Construction: 10,000 random composition pairs from MP-20 were generated, and GPT-4o was used to explain property changes between each pair. Compositional similarity was computed using the CBFV package, and the five most similar source compositions were retrieved for each query, reranked by the LLM, and the top three selected. (5) LLM Backbone Experiments: OpenAI GPT-4o and o3-mini were used as LLM backbones. 20 independent runs of 15 iterations each were conducted per configuration, starting from randomly sampled MP-20 compositions. Target formation energies were set at five quantile-defined values: -3.8, -3.5, -3.0, -2.5, and -1.6 eV/atom. (6) Ablation on Tools: Experiments were performed with and without tool-assisted Planning and Proposition for both LLMs, and each of the four tools (short-term memory, long-term memory, periodic table, knowledge base) was tested independently using GPT-4o. (7) Baseline Comparison: MatterGen, a diffusion-based generative model fine-tuned on MP-20 with classifier-free guidance, was used as a baseline. 256 compositions were generated per target condition and evaluated using the same property predictor, without structural relaxation post-processing. (8) Compositional Metrics Evaluation: Validity (SMACT), uniqueness, novelty (against MP-20), and the combined V.U.N. score were computed for generated compositions targeting -3.8 eV/atom. (9) Natural Language Constraint Experiments: Three practical constraint scenarios were tested using o3-mini with tools at target formation energies of -3.8 or -2.5 eV/atom: exclusion of environmentally hazardous elements (Pb, Hg, Cd, Cr), exclusion of actinides, and restriction to non-metal-only compositions, each imposed via natural language prompts. (10) Knowledge-Informed Initialization: Two alternative initialization methods were evaluated—LLM-based sampling (LLM proposes initial composition from a natural language prompt) and Retriever-based sampling (a T5 encoder trained via contrastive learning on MP-20 property and composition descriptions retrieves relevant initial compositions). These were compared against random initialization in terms of starting property values, success rates, and V.U.N. scores. (11) Reasoning Interpretability Analysis: Reasoning texts from Planning and Proposition stages were embedded using SciBERT, projected with t-SNE, and clustered with k-means to analyze patterns in LLM decision-making and tool selection for both GPT-4o and o3-mini.
